transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble with my eating habits lately. I hope it's okay to bring this up, but... after my cashier shifts, I've been picking up some takeout. 

And, well, it's... it's kind of a lot. I guess I just get really hungry after being on my feet, but I'll end up buying what looks like enough food for a whole family. Like, a bunch of burgers, fries, chicken, desserts... and I just sit there and eat almost all of it by myself before I even go home. It's just a bad habit, really, but it's pretty embarrassing to admit out loud. Is that... is that the kind of thing you can help me with?
When you're eating all of that food after work, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Um... I guess you could say that. I mean, it's not like I'm completely out of my mind or anything, I don't want you to think I'm crazy. But... yeah, it is a little hard to stop once I get going. 

I hope it's okay to explain it like this, but... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just kind of clicks off? And even while I'm sitting there telling myself, you know, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more,' my hands just... they just keep reaching for the next thing anyway. I really try to be good and stop myself, I promise I do, but it just happens. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
When you're eating all of that food after work, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?

Um... actually, no, I don't think so. I hope I'm not giving you the wrong answer or anything, but I haven't really noticed myself eating super fast. 

I mean, I'm not, like, frantically stuffing my face... I don't want you to picture anything gross like that. I just kind of eat at a normal pace, I guess? It just takes a while because... well, because there's a lot of it. But I really try to just eat it like a regular meal, just taking normal bites. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful answer.
Do you usually eat all of that food by yourself, and do you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating in front of others?

Um... yeah. I do. I hope you don't think less of me for this, but... I definitely do it by myself. I'm just really ashamed of it, honestly. I don't want to gross anyone out or make them uncomfortable. 

So, um, I'll usually just sit in my car in the parking lot and eat it there. Or, if I do bring things home, I'll wait until my wife is completely asleep. I just... I don't want her to see how much I had. I even take the bags and the receipts and I stuff them way down deep at the bottom of the trash so she won't find them. 

It sounds so sneaky when I say it out loud, and I'm really not a deceitful guy, I promise. I just get so embarrassed about the whole thing. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
When you're eating all of that food, do you often continue eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Um... yeah, I guess I do. I mean, I don't want it to sound like I'm completely gorging myself until I burst, I'm really trying not to do that. But... well, I do sometimes push it a bit too far. 

A lot of nights, I just keep going until my stomach gets really tight, and it actually hurts pretty bad. It's embarrassing to admit, but sometimes I have to lean the seat all the way back in my car, or if I'm at home, I just lie totally still in bed and wait for the pain to pass. I hope you don't think I'm just being gluttonous, I really don't mean to let it get to that point. I just... I don't realize how full I am until it's too late. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
How often do you find yourself eating an unusually large amount of food in one sitting, like the meals you described after work?

Um... gosh, I hope this doesn't sound too bad. I really try to be good, you know? But... well, for the last several months, it's been happening maybe... three or four nights most weeks. 

I mean, I don't want to make it sound like it's every single day or anything. It's just... things have been really stressful lately. Ever since the bank started calling about the foreclosure, I don't think there's been a single week where I didn't do it at least once. I'm really trying to get a handle on it, I promise. I just... it's a lot of pressure, you know? Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not coming across as totally out of control.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Um... well, it's not like it's completely ruining my whole life or anything. I mean, I still make it to all my cashier shifts on time, and I work really hard there. I'm trying my best to keep that part of things totally normal. 

But... yeah, it does cause me a lot of distress, honestly. I guess the hardest part is... well, with the foreclosure and everything, I'm spending money we just really don't have right now on all this extra food. And having to keep more and more secrets from my wife... it just makes everything at home feel so tense and dishonest. I hate feeling like I'm lying to her, I really do. I want to be a good partner to her. 

I hope you don't think I'm a terrible husband for doing this behind her back. I'm just struggling a bit to stop. Is... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories you consumed?

Um... oh, no. No, I definitely don't do anything like that. I mean, I know I really mess up with the eating part, but I've never tried to make myself throw up, or... or taken any laxatives or anything. I'd be really scared to try something like that, honestly. 

And as for exercise... well, I really don't exercise much at all right now. I know I probably should, just to be a healthier person, but I definitely don't do it excessively to burn off the food. I just sort of... let it sit there, even when it hurts. 

Is that... is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, I don't want to leave anything out if it's important.
Can you tell me if you ever feel like you’ve completely lost control over your eating during these episodes, like you can’t stop eating even if you wanted to?

Um... well, I really try to stay in control, I honestly do. I don't want you to think I'm just completely giving up or not trying at all. But... yeah, I guess it does feel a bit like that sometimes. 

It's just... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just sort of clicks off. And even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more,' my hands just keep reaching for the next thing. It's like I can't quite make myself stop in the moment, even when I know I really should. 

I'm so sorry if that sounds awful. I know I should be stronger than that. Is... is it normal to feel that way? I hope I'm explaining it okay, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
